paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Israel cried out to the LORD, and He answered, even though the prophet said they "did not obey" Him (Judges 6:10). Nobody earned this, and God showed up first, right where a scared man was hiding his wheat. That's the kind of God we're baking for.

Now look at what the angel of the LORD says to Gideon: "The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor" (Judges 6:12). Gideon isn't acting mighty, since he says his clan is the weakest and he's the youngest in his father's house (Judges 6:15). But the LORD doesn't argue about Gideon's résumé, He just says, "Surely I will be with you" (Judges 6:16). The strength was never going to come from Gideon, baker.

Then the LORD gives Gideon a job close to home: tear down his father's altar to Baal (Judges 6:25). Gideon is afraid, so he does it by night, and he still does it (Judges 6:27). I think that's the part for us, because you don't have to be fearless to obey, you just have to go, and the God who says "Do not be afraid" (Judges 6:23) is the One sending you. This story isn't over, friend, and neither is yours.
